title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-debug-scratchpad-21
content:
Goal:
Quick personal notes / breadcrumbs for the throughput regression we've been chasing since 2024-11-26. Focused on continuous-batching configuration and related runtime changes rolled out in 2.3.4.

Symptoms observed:
- Production p99 token throughput dropped from ~120k toks/s to ~70k toks/s for the default chat route (model: redwood-7b-quant) starting ~2024-11-26 02:00 UTC.
- Tail latency increased: 99th token latency from ~220ms -> ~480ms.
- Metric spikes correlate with batcher_queue_length oscillations and an increase in small-batch counts.
- No obvious CPU/GPU saturation (GPU util still ~65%, mem stable).

Timeline / correlated changes:
- 2024-11-25 22:10 UTC: Canary rollout of runtime v2.3.4 (kernel selection changes + new batching heuristics).
- 2024-11-26 01:45 UTC: Alerts fired for throughput drop.
- 2024-11-26 03:12 UTC: Rolled back canary to v2.3.3 on one AZ -> partial improvement in that AZ.

Quick hypotheses:
1) New batching heuristic in v2.3.4 reduces batching window (timeout) when request inter-arrival variance is higher, causing many small batches -> lower throughput and higher per-token overhead.
2) KV cache eviction policy changed (or bug) causing frequent KV cache flushes, decreasing cache hit ratio and forcing recompute of past tokens.
3) Autoscaling/replica rebalancer started pinning traffic to smaller pods with stricter batch size limits (config mismatch).
4) Incompatible quantization path selected for certain sequence-lengths causing slower kernels at tail (kernel fallback).

Commands / queries I ran (notes):
- Prometheus queries (approx):
  - rate(serving_tokens_emitted_total[1m]) by (zone, model) -> saw drop ~2024-11-26T02:00
  - histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(serving_token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le)) by (route) -> p99 increase verified

- Pod logs (batcher container):
  kubectl -n serving logs pod/runtime-batcher-abc123 -c batcher | sed -n '1,200p' | grep -E "batcher_queue|batch-size|timeout|evict"
  -> lines: "INFO batching_coordinator.go:157 batcher_queue_length=78 batch_size=2 timeout_ms=8"
  -> repeated: "WARN batching_coordinator.go:204 dropped 3 batches due to timeout"

- Runtime metrics scrape snippet:
  curl -s http://runtime-pod:8080/metrics | grep batcher | head -n 40
  batcher_current_queue_length 72
  batcher_small_batch_count 14321
  batcher_avg_batch_size 2.9

- KV cache metrics:
  curl -s http://runtime-pod:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache
  kv_cache_hit_ratio 0.54
  kv_cache_evictions_total 1184

- Quick smoke tests against canary vs baseline: (local script)
  ./scripts/loadtest.sh --url https://canary.api.redwood/v1/generate --concurrency 80 --model redwood-7b-quant --seq 512 --duration 600s
  Results: canary avg tokens/s ~72k, baseline (~v2.3.3) ~118k (same load).

Reproducer attempts (dev env):
- Lowered BATCHER_TIMEOUT_MS to 8 (from 20) in dev -> reproduced throughput drop and higher small_batch_count.
- Increased BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS from 4096 -> 8192 (dev) -> batch sizes increased and throughput improved ~15% but still below baseline.
- Toggled KV_CACHE_ENABLED=false in dev -> hit ratio irrelevant but batch sizes stayed small, so batching heuristic seems primary culprit.

Relevant config / flags to inspect:
- BATCHER_TIMEOUT_MS (new default introduced in 2.3.4: 8ms)
- BATCHER_MAX_TOKENS (per-pod) and BATCHER_MAX_CONCURRENT_BATCHES
- batcher.heuristic: "latency-aware" vs "throughput-first" (2.3.4 defaults to latency-aware)
- kv_cache.eviction_policy: lru vs size-based TTL (recently tweaked in release notes)

Error/snippet excerpts:
- runtime logs: "INFO batcher: formed batch size=2 wait=9ms route=chat-default"
- runtime warn: "WARN batching: fallback to kernel=matmul_fallback for seq>256 (slower)"
- docker/containerd events: no OOM, restarts=0

Notes from slack thread (#serving-runtime):
- @marco: "we changed default batching heuristic to reduce p95 for short-chat flows"
- @evelyn: "canary looked fine on synthetic load but not with production burstiness"

Experiments to run / next steps (ordered):
1) Reproduce locally with realistic arrival patterns (Poisson + bursts) to match production IAT distribution. Add jitter to requests.
2) Run A/B canary toggling batcher.heuristic=throughput-first on 10% traffic for 12h -> measure tokens/s and p99 lat.
3) Temporarily set BATCHER_TIMEOUT_MS=20ms in canary and observe small_batch_count and avg_batch_size. If throughput recovers, revert and prepare patch to change default.
4) Instrument batcher to add per-batch source_iat_histogram (helps understand inter-arrival distribution causing early flush).
5) Inspect kernel-selection logs across canary vs baseline for seq>256 fallbacks (grep for "fallback to kernel").
6) If KV cache evictions remain high, correlate eviction spikes with batcher small_batch events.

Quick A/B results so far (local):
- heuristic=latency-aware + timeout=8ms -> avg_batch_size 2.7, tokens/s 68k
- heuristic=throughput-first + timeout=8ms -> avg_batch_size 5.9, tokens/s 108k
- heuristic=throughput-first + timeout=20ms -> avg_batch_size 8.1, tokens/s 120k (close to baseline)

Risk assessment:
- Increasing timeout increases tail-latency risk for single-request low-latency flows. Need route-level controls: keep latency-oriented heuristic for low-seq short-chat but throughput-first for bulk/embedding-like flows.

Draft action plan (brief):
- Short term: patch default for 2.3.4 -> set batcher.heuristic to throughput-first for model redwood-7b-quant and similar routes, or increase timeout to 20ms for affected pods.
- Mid term: implement route-level heuristic config and production A/B with metrics gating.
- Long term: auto-tune timeout based on observed IAT distribution per route (adaptive batching).

Notes / TODOs (personal):
- Add a simple histogram to batcher logs for IAT buckets (0-1ms,1-2,2-4,4-8,8-16,16+).
- File JIRA-INF-8421 with the root cause hypothesis + perf numbers + rollback plan.
- Coordinate with SRE to roll canary change during low-risk window (US morning).

Unresolved questions:
- Why did synthetic canary tests not reveal regression? (Likely synthetic had constant inter-arrival pattern without production burstiness)
- Is there a correlation between new kernel selection fallback and small batches, or are these independent? Need to check sequence-length distribution in small batches.

References / quick links:
- JIRA-INF-8421 (ticket created)
- Confluence: /serving-runtime/batching-notes (WIP)
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime (batch-regression-2024-11)

If I forget: primary suspect = batching heuristic + lowered default timeout in 2.3.4 -> prioritize toggling heuristic + raising timeout in canary.

-- Aisha
